newsitem.title: USA: Major stock movements overnight - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: Major stock movements overnight - Sept 26.

text.p: NEW YORK - The Dow Jones industrial average fell Wednesday, hit for a second day by the gyrations of powerhouse AT&T Corp after the telecommunications giant warned that its earnings will disappoint Wall Street.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the 30-stock Dow index was off 5.55 points at 5,868.48. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on moderate volume of 258 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

AT&T, whose stock if the most widely owned in North America, warned on Tuesday that competition in its key long-distance telephone market would likely result in profit shortfalls for the second half of the year.
The announcement prompted several brokerage houses to downgrade the stock of the telecommunications giant. AT&T was down 1/2 at 51 after tumbling 5-3/4 on Tuesday.

LONDON - Shares bounced from three days of losses, tracking higher bonds in the wake of the U.S. decision to leave interest rates unchanged. A shaky start on Wall Street pulled the FTSE 100 index below the day's best and by the close the FTSE 100 was up 25.2 points at 3,935.7, below the day's peak.

FRANKFURT - Blue-chip shares hit new record highs amid a wave of short-covering and some genuine buying after the Federal Reserve's unexpected decision to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged. The 30-share DAX closed the bourse session up 20.52 points at 2,658.97, sailing past an old record at 2,650.49 and set a new all-time intraday high of 2,659.66. The IBIS index of all-day electronic trade nudged slightly higher in late dealings, ending at 2,663.10 after touching 2,665.65.

PARIS - Stocks rose more than one percent, lifting the CAC-40 index to a close above the 2,100 level, on investor relief that the U.S. did not raise its interest rates. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 21.91 points, or 1.05 percent, at 2,103.41, helped by rising bond markets.

ZURICH - Shares closed higher on the day but below midday highs. Dealers said the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged calmed the market. The all-share SPI added 21.38 points, or 0.91 percent, to close at 2,370.77.

TOKYO - Stocks closed higher, mainly encouraged by institutional investors' buying in the semiconductor sector. But many brokers said that the chip market has not yet bottomed out and that it was not likely to continue keeping the whole market afloat. The key Nikkei 225 average gained 178.68 points or 0.84 percent to close at 21,350.67.

HONG KONG - Stocks ended on a firm note, although well off the day's highs, after rotational trade in blue chip shares. Brokers said investors took the opportunity to do some portfolio re-positioning, selling underperformers and outperformers now
that interest rate uncertainty had been eased by the U.S. decision on Tuesday to hold rates steady. The Hang Seng Index rose 56.83 points to 11,603.53.

SYDNEY - The share market sprinted home to end at its day's high as buyers re-emerged after metal prices firmed overseas and bonds rallied as the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged. The All Ordinaries index rose 24.1 points to 2,252.8. Brokers said local investors had taken heart from interest rate developments in the U.S. and gold and base metals prices that showed signs of a rebound, at least in the short term.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended strong in active trade, with gold shares off their best levels but still firm on a brighter bullion price and industrials firm on positive sentiment. Dealers said the market was surprisingly strong after expectations of a weak opening. The overall index gained 41.9 points to 6,959.8 points, the industrial index added 33.1 points to 8,204 and the gold index was up 29.4 points to 1,751.
